acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Permission consent and capture-stop controls use Rust/Metal text, dialog actions and panel allocation, with explicit native request/decision/device/OS/window/event/focus/AX adapters.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: The opt-in permission body replaces native DialogModelHost paragraphs with shared scene text and Rust panel allocation. The action row reuses Rust pointer/key state, Metal drawing and native default-button/input-protection/focus/AX adapters. Requesting, permission and embedding origins, capabilities and profile metadata preserve their original conditions and strings.

The actual Chromium PermissionPrompt, PermissionRequestManager and native State::Decide authority remain unchanged. Temporary/persistent grant eligibility, deny/dismiss, default Cancel and destroy-prompt/keep-pending tab-switch behavior remain native. Rendering or enabled state never grants a request.

A client-owned MediaSceneDialog holds delegate/widget/scene. The scene is destroyed before native closure; widget and delegate destruction is deferred off the executing button/decision callback stack. Native permission decisions and capture Stop stay synchronous. Only presentation adapter destruction is deferred; no delayed grant/stop command is introduced.

Capture controls reuse the scene bubble in a nonmodal mode with original fixed width, native close button, no capped scroll wrapper and no close-on-deactivate. The modal mode retains its original scroll workaround, margins and behavior for password, folder and workspace dialogs. Both modes retain the native title/frame/window and rounded client layer.

Capture stop callbacks keep their active generation token and weak PageMediaAccess target. Forced native closure stops the original capture once, then cleans its matching UI; programmatic close/refresh clears the active token before closure and never issues another Stop. Old close callbacks cannot clear a newer indicator. Native attribution, stream callbacks, desktop picker, OS checks and profile security remain untouched.

A new shared browser case checks default Cancel and unbound macOS Return, actual Cocoa Escape denial and Space allow after successful presentation, visible origin text, childless controls, no managed Label/MdTextButton, nonmodal close affordance, forced close ending real synthetic tracks, fresh same-origin capture and Space stop. Devices are synthetic; the permission manager and UI are real.

The existing combined camera/microphone consent/profile/one-time-grant case now verifies the capture scene remains visible while its page is in another workspace and stops it using actual Cocoa Space. Existing navigation teardown, cross-origin attribution, desktop picker cancel/filter/document lifetime and OS-denial cases remain in both gates.

No dependencies or browser-service policy changes were added. Native window/frame/scroll/View/Button/event/focus/AX nodes, permission presentation copy/coordination, other panels, manual acceptance, controlled profiling and release/license acceptance remain open.

first_probe.reason: The new assertion inspected native frame title Labels outside the managed body. The new forced-close test also stopped as soon as the indicator registered, before the page getUserMedia promise necessarily installed ended listeners; both backends then waited for an event the page could miss. The test now scopes checks to delegate contents and waits for the page running state before either stop. A 30-second stage-reporting timeout was added. Production source is unchanged after the probe.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.

limits: Native titles/frames and modal/scroll/window/event/focus/AX containers, other forms/panels/layouts and remaining form construction/service wording remain open. Native browser validation, authority, stores and operations remain explicit adapters.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, global RTL, typography/scale/pixel fidelity, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup or memory improvement is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
